items.title: Prosperity Gap estimates, by region
items.content:
| Region | 1990 | 1995 | 2000 | 2005 | 2010 | 2015 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| East Asia and Pacific | 16.5 | 13.0 | 11.5 | 8.06 | 6.26 | 4.06 | 3.25 | 3.28 | 3.04 | 3.00 | 2.92 | 2.83 |

| Eastern and Southern Africa | 17.0 | 18.7 | 19.0 | 17.0 | 14.4 | 13.5 | -- | 14.7 | 14.5 | 14.3 | 14.2 | 14.1 |

| World | 10.9 | 9.96 | 9.43 | 7.81 | 6.55 | 5.58 | 5.12 | 5.28 | 5.16 | 5.07 | 5.00 | 4.93 |

Source: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform (version September 2024), https://pip.worldbank.org.
Note: The estimates for Middle East and North Africa and Eastern and Southern Africa are projected starting in 2019. Western and Central Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa are projected starting in 2020. All other regions are projected in 2023 and 2024. For further details on projection, see annex 1A of chapter 1. Gray shading = projected estimate.
